abstract: Chegg, an online learning platform, eliminated 636 employees through two rounds of layoffs occurring in 2024 and early 2025, reducing its workforce by approximately 67% from peak levels. The company's CEO explicitly identified artificial intelligence as an existential threat to its homework-help business model, driving the restructuring efforts.
keyFindings: Chegg eliminated 636 employees across two rounds of layoffs in 2024 and early 2025.
The first round of layoffs accounted for 23% of the workforce in 2024, with additional cuts in early 2025.
Total workforce reduction reached approximately 67% of peak employment levels.
CEO cited AI as an existential threat to the company's homework-help business model.
methodology: SEC filing and press release from Chegg announcing restructuring plan dated February 1, 2025. Source provides official company disclosure of layoff figures and strategic rationale.
qualifiers: The exact percentage breakdown of the second round of layoffs is not specified; only the combined total of 636 employees and ~67% of peak workforce reduction are stated. The specific timeline and implementation details of the early 2025 cuts are not detailed in the excerpt provided.
